resale_co.name: Continued Certificate of Occupancy (CCO), residential sale
resale_co.issued_by: Linden Health Department (residential Certificate of Occupancy inspections); the Construction Code office handles commercial CCOs
requirements: Owner certifies the dwelling and all other structures meet the City's zoning requirements
No rubbish, debris or bulk garbage may be left on the property before the new occupancy
resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online with the City's GovPilot 'Residential Sale CCO Application' (Residential Sale Only), linked from the City's Continued Certificate of Occupancy Application page. The form asks for the buyer, the agent and who to contact for inspections, and offers Pay Now or Submit & Pay Later. Questions go to the Health Department, 605 South Wood Avenue, (908) 474-8409.

resale_co.notes: Linden runs a residential-sale Continued Certificate of Occupancy through its Health Department (the Construction Code page says residential C/Os come through Housing). No residential fee, inspection checklist, lead time or validity was found on an official page, and the GovPilot form computes the fee only at checkout. The City's code is on ecode360 (LI4062), which could not be opened. The $200 fee on the City's 2020 'Application for Continued Certificate of Occupancy' is the Construction Code (commercial/business) CCO, not the residential sale CCO. Linden also has Rental Property Registration and a lead hazard program for pre-1978 rentals through the Health Department; those are rental programs, not resale requirements.

requirements: Smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed battery or hardwired, on each level including basements (not attics or crawl spaces) and outside each separate sleeping area within 10 feet of the bedrooms
Carbon monoxide alarms outside each sleeping area
Hardwired (A/C-powered) smoke alarms from the original construction may not be replaced with battery alarms

Homes with a secondary power source (generator, solar panels, battery storage) need a 'CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER' label (not handwritten) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and the electric meter
A property representative or homeowner must be present at the inspection; a no-show counts as a failure

authorities.name: City of Linden Fire Department, Fire Prevention Bureau
authorities.lead_time: Apply more than 10 business days before the change of occupancy for the lowest fee. A new application is required if the sale does not happen within six months.

fees.label: Certificate of smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm compliance, request received more than 10 business days before the change of occupancy
fees.quote: 1). Requests for a CSDCMAC received more than 10 business days prior to the change of occupancy: $50.00

fees.label: Certificate, request received 4 to 10 business days before the change of occupancy
fees.quote: 2). Requests for a CSDCMAC received 4 to 10 business days prior to the change of occupancy: $90.00

fees.label: Certificate, request received fewer than 4 business days before the change of occupancy (cash only)
fees.quote: 3). Requests for a CSDCMAC received fewer than four business days prior to the change of occupancy: $170.00(CASH ONLY)

authorities.how_to_apply: Download the Smoke Detector & Carbon Monoxide Application Form from the City website, fill it out and mail it or drop it in the bin outside the Fire Prevention entrance, 302 South Wood Avenue, Monday to Friday 9 am to 5 pm. Checks payable to City of Linden (the under-4-business-days fee is cash only). The bureau schedules the inspection as soon as possible after it gets the application.
authorities.contact_title: Deputy Chief/Fire Official (the Fire Prevention page's email belongs to Fire Chief William M. Hasko, Jr.)
